title: WPSS/117/2016 of Vandana Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No.1348 of 2014
Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J.
 Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate, for
the petitioner.
 Mr. B.S. Parihar, S.C., for the State.
 Mr. Siddhartha Sah, Advocate, for
the respondent no.3.
 Petitioner was appointed on daily-wage basis. He made a representation
seeking regularization. In view of the
representation made by the petitioner, the
respondent no.3 sent a recommendation to
respondent no.2 vide letter dated
22.2.2012. The respondent no.2 raised
certain defects vide communication dated
1.6.2012. Respondent no.3 again sent a
communication after removing the defects
on 8.11.2012. However, no steps were
taken. The respondent no.3 then sent a
reminder. The respondent no.2 sent a
communication to the State Govt. on
26.3.2014, contending therein, that in the
Regularization Rules, 2011, there is no
mention of the institutions under Grant-in-Aid List. The State Govt. has not taken
any decision qua respondent no.3-
institution but with regard to other
institutions, the State Government has
issued the Government Order on
19.7.2013 (Annexure No.11).
 The petitioner cannot be
discriminated against by the State.
 Learned Counsel for the respondent
no.3 has vehemently argued that the case
of the petitioner cannot be considered for
regularization. The stand taken by the
Counsel for the respondent no.3 before this
Court is contrary to the pleadings. The
respondent no.3, all throughout, has
supported the case of petitioner by making
successive recommendations to the
respondent no.3. The stand taken by the
respondent no.3 is just diametrical
opposite to the pleadings.

Accordingly, the petition is allowed
with costs quantified as Rs.10,000/- (ten
thousand only) as against the respondent
no.3. The respondent nos.1 and 2 are
directed to consider the case of petitioner
for regularization in view of successive
recommendations made by the respondent
no.3 vide communications dated
22.2.2012, 19.11.2013 read with G.O.
dated 19.7.2013, within ten weeks from
today.
 All pending applications stand
disposed of.
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.)
 08.05.2018
Rdang
